claims.title: Per-principal attribution
claims.maturity_note: Scope: 'supported' covers the store-level cryptographic property — every event is bound to the principal whose Ed25519 key signed it, and a spoofed actor, a wrong key, or a revoked key is detected. It does NOT assert that the dossier web layer derives actor_id from an authenticated session rather than a client-supplied value (residual T3, below); that is a separate web-authentication concern tracked under dossier's auth surface, not this claim. Suite interop drives the canonical workflow end-to-end with per-principal Ed25519 signing at both spine and face level (tests/test_interop.py::test_drive_work_item_per_principal_ed25519_to_done and ..._across_real_faces; the face-level proof requires agent-notes and dossier installed in CI, INTEROP_REQUIRE_FACES=1). The project is created strict_asymmetric=True so HMAC fallback is rejected; every event is asserted per-transition to carry scheme_id ed25519, the acting principal as actor_id, and the matching ed-<principal> key_id. Per-event verify_event_principal_binding (which fails on unregistered-signer / signature mismatch, unlike replay's binding pass that silently skips unregistered actors) and chain-level replay(verify_principal_binding=True) verify against the principal_keys registry with zero binding failures; each event verifies under its own principal's exported public key and under no other principal's key; revocation of a principal's key makes its past events fail binding with key-revoked, surfaced by both the per-event API and replay. The shipped faces (agent-notes RegistaFace, dossier RegistaGateway) sign per-principal transparently and dossier's read path + verify_event surface the scheme and principal binding. Residuals: T3 (dossier session->actor_id binding untested in agent-suite CI) and T1 (a compromised signing proxy can forge validly-signed events — attribution proves who signed, not that the signatory intended the action).

claims.title: Key rotation safety
claims.maturity_note: The v6 proof is chain-ordered and non-retroactive: a signed principal_key_acceptance_revoked makes the principal's next write fail with KEY_ACCEPTANCE_REVOKED, while events written before the revocation remain valid because their acceptance was live when they were signed (tests/test_adversarial_corpus.py::test_adversarial_mutation[REVOKED_KEY]). The projection-registry verifier is explicitly refused for v6 and is not evidence for this claim. Still provisional: a full rotate (new key signs new events while the old key's earlier events remain valid, and replay(verify_principal_binding=True) succeeds over the mixed pre/post-rotation chain) is not yet a CI assertion.
